title: Moving Quietly
question: Does a cross-system connection fit a specific management task or extend beyond it?
briefing: A management identity connected from the orchestration service to an archive host. Cross-system administration is routine at Northstar; the connection alone is not a finding. Your authority is to acquire records and recommend a session-scoped response through Platform Operations. You cannot approve your own control or disable an entire account or service.
lesson: A lateral access path describes one system reaching another; its legitimacy depends on task, target and authority.

entities.name: Archive-host management session
entities.impact: The archive host supports daily restore validation. There is no authority to isolate it directly or interrupt unrelated backup paths.
entities.capability: Named session and disclosed source paths only; no account-wide or host-wide control.
entities.dependency: The archive host supports daily restore validation. There is no authority to isolate it directly or interrupt unrelated backup paths.

entities.name: ORCH-06 context
entities.purpose: Related context that must be assessed separately
entities.impact: Do not generalise the primary session finding to this separate scope.
entities.capability: Only the explicitly delivered relationship and source records.
entities.dependency: A separate task or observation does not supply approval for the primary session.

mechanic.question: Does a cross-system connection fit a specific management task or extend beyond it?

options.label: Treat all administrative cross-system access as misuse
Follow the acquired path and compare the actual target with the task
Decide from the management tool name

limits.label: A management connection or tool name alone is not evidence of unauthorised movement.
Unavailable collection does not establish that no activity occurred.
The source identifies a session or credential, not a person or motive.
Other scopes and their remaining questions need their own evidence.

queries.label: Establish the task and business consequence
queries.question: What is this service for, and which consequences change investigation priority?
queries.can: Names the normal task, related scopes, owners and interruption consequence.
queries.cannot: Does not establish who performed the current action.

queries.label: Check the exact work authorisation
queries.question: Does approved work cover this session, task, target and period?
queries.cannot: Does not prove the human operator or the activity that actually occurred.

queries.label: Inspect the scoped session activity
queries.question: Which action was recorded for this named session within collection limits?
queries.can: Records session-level actions and the observed target.
queries.cannot: Cannot identify a person, establish motive or reconstruct missing historical collection.

queries.label: Check the service transaction independently
queries.question: Does the service-side transaction establish the same scoped operation?
queries.can: Tests the operation through a separately collected service transaction.
queries.cannot: A second card alone does not establish a sufficient explanation.

facts.title: Starting observations
facts.text: A management identity connected from the orchestration service to an archive host. Cross-system administration is routine at Northstar; the connection alone is not a finding.

facts.title: Task, scope and business consequence
facts.text: The documented management path is ORCH-06 → archive service → restore-check dataset. The identity may validate restores but may not retrieve unrelated payroll archives.

facts.title: The specific work authorisation
facts.text: The maintenance work order explicitly covers the archive session, restore-check dataset and management path for this review period.

facts.title: Recorded session activity
facts.text: The archive session followed the documented management path and read the restore-check dataset named in the work order.

facts.title: An independently collected transaction
facts.text: The archive service independently logged the restore-check dataset request and the approved orchestration origin for the named session.

facts.title: Verified business-context response
facts.text: A pre-established directory contact confirmed the task record: The maintenance work order explicitly covers the archive session, restore-check dataset and management path for this review period. This confirms the business record, not the person operating the session.

facts.title: The specific work authorisation
facts.text: The maintenance work order covers restore checks only; it grants no access to payroll archives through the archive session.

facts.title: Recorded session activity
facts.text: The archive session reached an additional payroll dataset outside the restore-check task. The source establishes this access path and target, not a general network-wide compromise.

facts.title: An independently collected transaction
facts.text: The archive access audit independently recorded the payroll-dataset request from the named archive session, beyond the documented management route.

facts.title: Verified business-context response
facts.text: A pre-established directory contact confirmed the task record: The maintenance work order covers restore checks only; it grants no access to payroll archives through the archive session. This confirms the business record, not the person operating the session.

facts.title: Work record unavailable
facts.text: The work-authorisation archive is unavailable for the named session and period. No approval or denial can be inferred.

facts.title: Session collection unavailable
facts.text: The session-audit source did not collect the relevant historical interval. Absence of a record cannot establish the absence of activity.

facts.title: Independent collection is limited
facts.text: The independent service journal lacks the target application operation for the historical interval. A different source name does not restore that capability.

facts.title: Verified check timed out
facts.text: The pre-established directory contact did not respond by the stated due step. This is a delivered limitation, not approval or a reason to wait indefinitely.

facts.title: A later scoped transaction
facts.text: The named session performed a further source-recorded operation within the specifically approved task. This later event does not identify the person, establish motive or change any earlier snapshot.
